_comment: Every navigation-relevant number the engine uses — Aneesh/SIH-IDR-android.md §10: 'No numeric constant relevant to navigation appears in Kotlin source.' See EngineConfig.kt for what each field means and where the value came from.
_comment_blend_cap: The absolute speed model may inform the estimate but must not own it. Measured on 238 s of motorbike riding (1,704 labelled windows): r-squared 0.037 against true speed, MAE 2.84 m/s, where simply predicting the median scores 1.46 — the model is WORSE than a constant on this vehicle. Uncapped, lam reaches 1 and the model fully replaces the constant-velocity prior during a long outage. Raise this only when a retrain beats a constant on the target vehicle. TODO K12.
_comment_blend_cap_bike: The model is trained AND validated on cars (IO-VNBD, R2 0.66). On a motorbike it scores R2 0.037, MAE 2.84 m/s, against 1.46 for predicting the median — worse than ignoring the sensors. Trust it where it was validated, distrust it where it was measured to fail. Raise this the moment a retrain beats a constant on a two-wheeler. TODO L4.
_comment_handling: ZUPT is a floor test only — shaking the phone exceeds its thresholds and disables it. HandlingDetector is the missing ceiling: mean gyro rate PERPENDICULAR to gravity, which a vehicle body cannot sustain and a hand cannot avoid. 0.44 rad/s = 25 deg/s, argued from vehicle physics and not yet fitted — telemetry logs tilt_rate_rps every tick so a real drive can replace it. See TODO.md G1.
_comment_handling_gate: MEASURE-ONLY for the first vehicle drive (TODO.md H9). The gate has never seen a car, and a false positive holds speed and freezes heading — which would corrupt the drive it is meant to be calibrated against. tilt_rate_rps and handling are still logged every tick. Turn on once a drive shows the distribution, same as use_gnss_nis_gate and use_map_match_fusion.
_comment_delta: OFF. FeatureExtractor emits a_horiz as a MAGNITUDE, so the sign of longitudinal acceleration is gone before the delta model sees it — accelerating and braking are the same input. Verified: a hard-braking window returns +0.30 m/s^2 where truth is -2.5. Field: +0.01 m/s^2 regardless of what the vehicle did. Needs a signed longitudinal channel and a retrain, not a config change. TODO K2.
_comment_variance: AI in the FUSION step (PS deliverable 4), not just upstream of it. When the loaded model has a heteroscedastic variance head, its per-window uncertainty replaces the hand-tuned ekf_speed_noise_mps for that tick — a model that knows it is guessing widens the filter instead of being trusted at a constant. Harmless before the head exists: models without one report no uncertainty and the filter falls back. TODO K7.
_comment_tick_dt: The engine integrates REAL elapsed time, not a nominal 1/rate. Measured tick spacing was p50 99ms / p90 212ms / p99 647ms, so the fixed dt lost 20.5% of elapsed time and was masking the speed model error. This bounds how much a single late tick may integrate. TODO K1.
_comment_gnss_gate: Escalating acceptance, not a binary gate. Strict 30 m while fixes flow; after gnss_starved_after_s with nothing accepted, fixes up to the ceiling pass through with their real accuracy. The old hardcoded binary 30 m gate locked GNSS out for 2h11m of an indoor session (9 sats in view, every fix >30 m) while the engine dead-reckoned 1.4 km of drift.
_comment_mapfuse: ON as of 2026-09-01 (TODO K10). The 15 m uncertainty gate passes 90% of ticks on a real ride, but a high pass rate means the matcher is CONFIDENT, not CORRECT — on a dense grid it was visibly following wrong streets. map_match_max_heading_disagree_deg is the correctness check that makes enabling this defensible: a road we are actually on has a bearing near our heading (or its reverse).
_comment_ekf_noise: Filter noise terms. ekf_heading_arw_deg_per_sqrt_s is the one to revisit first: it is fitted to aggregate cross-track medians, not measured, and a real stationary-phone Allan variance should replace it (architecture doc §11). Raising it makes the filter less confident; use_gnss_nis_gate and use_map_match_fusion both stay off until that number is measured.
_comment_road_bearing: Road bearing as a heading measurement. The pre-EKF engine nudged the gyro heading toward the matched road (road_heading_gain); that path is inert whenever the EKF owns heading, so this re-enters the same correction as a weighted measurement under the same gates. Heading only, never position.
_comment_mag_heading: Compass as a heading measurement, with the phone-to-vehicle mount offset solved as a filter state. OFF: unlike use_road_bearing_heading this is a new fusion input, not a restored one, and the magnetometer is the sensor the integration contract excluded for vehicle distortion. Turn it on after a drive where (mag_heading_deg - heading) looks steady per mount at mag_accuracy = 3, then watch mount_offset_deg converge.
_comment_yaw_bike: A leaning two-wheeler out-rotates a car body. Measured on a motorbike: projected yaw reached 190 deg/s, and samples above the 90 bound sat INSIDE genuine turns (mean 41 deg/s around them), not isolated vibration — the bound was cutting real turn dynamics, ~5 deg per 4.4 min. 200 is above a real turn and below the 271 deg/s recorded while walking, which is what the bound exists to reject. TODO K11.
